prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Solar PV capacity additions by country and quarter, 2024 (MW) (language en).
Grid: 9 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Segment" spans 1 col × 3 row; "Europe" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Asia-Pacific" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Germany" spans 2 col × 1 row; "France" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Japan" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Australia" spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Segment" · longest unbreakable word 86px · one-line width 172px
  col 2: header "Europe › Germany › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 3: header "Europe › Germany › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 4: header "Europe › France › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 33px · one-line width 33px
  col 5: header "Europe › France › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 6: header "Asia-Pacific › Japan › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 7: header "Asia-Pacific › Japan › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 8: header "Asia-Pacific › Australia › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 9: header "Asia-Pacific › Australia › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 606px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 605px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare quarterly solar PV capacity additions (MW) for 2024 across five market segments and four countries, including Q1→Q2 movement and quarterly totals. It is a reference/comparison table, read row-wise (one segment across all countries) and pair-wise (Q1 vs Q2 within a country).","reading":"A reader anchors on the row label (segment), then sweeps right to compare the same segment across Germany, France, Japan and Australia, and compares the adjacent Q1/Q2 pair to see quarterly growth. Totals are read last as a column summary. Alignment is numeric/right, so columns must be at least wide enough that four-digit values with thousands separators never wrap or truncate; country and quarter headers are short and must stay on one line.","groups":["Col 1: row-label column (Segment) — a single anchor column, must be readable as a unit","Cols 2–3: Germany Q1/Q2 — an inseparable comparison pair","Cols 4–5: France Q1/Q2 — pair","Cols 6–7: Japan Q1/Q2 — pair","Cols 8–9: Australia Q1/Q2 — pair","Cols 2–5 together form the Europe block; cols 6–9 form the Asia-Pacific block, so the boundary between col 5 and col 6 should read as the strongest internal break"],"keep_intact":["All MW values, especially 4-digit totals (2,065 / 2,330 / 1,232 / 1,803) — never wrap or clip","Q1 and Q2 header tokens","Country names Germany / France / Japan / Australia","The row-label words 'Commercial', 'industrial', 'Residential', 'Utility-scale', 'Community' must not break mid-word"],"may_wrap":["Row-label phrases in col 1 ('Residential rooftop', 'Commercial & industrial', 'Utility-scale', 'Community solar') can break at the space/ampersand into two lines, absorbing extra height in already-tall body rows","Nothing in cols 2–9 should wrap; those columns are numeric and must stay one line"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [118, 62, 62, 61, 61, 61, 61, 59, 60] · table 606×361px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 60, 60, 36, 60, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/15 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [123, 62, 62, 59, 60, 60, 60, 59, 60] · table 606×361px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 60, 60, 36, 60, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/15 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [117, 62, 62, 62, 62, 60, 60, 60, 60] · table 606×361px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 60, 60, 36, 60, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/15 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
